Attachments: I attached a small SLO template (acme_slo_requirements.xlsx) and our latency playbook excerpt (redwood_latency-playbook.pdf).

- KV/prefix caching for common intro/knowledge prompts to avoid repeated decoding cost.
- Quantization profiles: evaluate 8-bit PTQ, 4/6-bit QAT candidates on quality/regression tests.

Thanks Sam — great questions. Short answers up front, then recommended config and what we’ll measure in the perf sims.

Q: Does continuous batching hurt first-token latency (TTFB)?
A: Not if implemented with priority/first-token reservation. Our runtime supports hybrid scheduling:
- First-token reservation path: small priority batches (or single-request fast-path) for first N tokens to meet TTFB SLOs.
- Larger batches for subsequent tokens to amortize decode cost.
We’ll run sims that explicitly measure TTFB p95 with hybrid batching enabled.

Recommended leverset we’ll evaluate (and what we expect to measure):
1) Adaptive continuous batching
   - Behavior: variable batch widths based on instantaneous QPS + first-token reservations.
   - Metric impact: large wins on throughput/unit-cost; small risk to TTFB if misconfigured.
2) Prefix/KV caching
   - Behavior: cache repeated prompt prefixes and common dialogue turns in memory (per-tenant, TTL configurable).
   - Metric impact: reduces avg tokens decoded per request and improves tail latency for cached flows.
3) Quantization profiles
   - Behavior: test 8-bit PTQ (lowest risk), 6-bit QAT candidate (medium), and 4-bit aggressive (high risk).
   - Metric impact: big cost savings with higher quantization; must run quality/regression evals (we’ll include your safety checks).
4) Model variants & routing
   - Behavior: route hot traffic to a lower-latency variant (e.g., quantized-13B) and reserve a higher-quality 34B for fallback/long-form or safety-critical paths.
   - Metric impact: reduces overall unit cost while preserving quality for sensitive cases.
5) Dedicated capacity vs Hosted API
   - Behavior: Dedicated reserved GPU pools yield more consistent p95 and allow pre-warmed KV caches; hosted can be cheaper for low sustained QPS.
   - Metric impact: Dedicated reduces tail variability (good for strict p95 targets).

What we’ll deliver from perf sims (expected turnaround ~5 business days after sample/data receipt):
- p50/p95/p99 for first-token and 512-token completions across candidate configs (batching+streaming+quantization+model variants).
- Cost estimate (USD per 1M tokens) per config, with an expected range and sensitivity to QPS.
- Regression flagging: pass/fail against your supplied safety/regression prompt set.
- Recommendation: 2 recommended configurations (fast-low-cost / high-quality-fallback) and a suggested rollout plan (canary -> regional pinning).

Action items:
- Acme: send sample prompts + regression set + any hard budget ceilings.
- Redwood: we’ll kick off sims, include rishi and priyom for pricing/engineering.
- Schedule: follow-up readout w/ perf numbers and pricing on Tue 12 Jan or Wed 13 Jan — which works for you?

Thanks — I’ll start the sims as soon as we have the sample.

Best,
Marissa
